key_insight: LongE2V shows that a pre-trained video diffusion model can be adapted to event streams to produce sharper, more stable long-horizon video reconstruction, prediction, and frame interpolation. The key breakthrough is using strong generative priors to overcome the blur and instability common in regression-based and earlier generative approaches.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of recovering high-quality video from sparse event data over long time horizons, where existing methods either blur fine details or drift and degrade over time.
method: Fine-tunes a foundational video diffusion model to learn from event-based inputs with high data efficiency.
Uses the diffusion prior to jointly support three tasks: video reconstruction, future frame prediction, and frame interpolation.
Introduces an autoregressive long-horizon strategy to improve temporal stability and preserve perceptual quality across extended sequences.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical route to better event-to-video systems without training massive models from scratch. For practitioners, it suggests diffusion priors can improve fidelity and long-range consistency in sparse-sensor video applications.

paper_title: LongE2V: Long-Horizon Event-based Video Reconstruction, Prediction, and Frame Interpolation with Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Cheng-De Fan, Chun-Wei Tuan Mu, Chen-Wei Chang, Chin-Yang Lin, Kun-Ru Wu
